comment: Every GNOME API this extension depends on, so a target shell version can be
checked before it is claimed in metadata.json. Kept by hand rather than
derived from the source: the point is to state the dependency deliberately,
and a grep cannot tell an API we rely on from a string that merely looks
like one.
'introspected' entries live in a typelib and can be resolved for real.
'shellInternals' are private JavaScript inside gnome-shell, which no
typelib describes, so they are searched for in the shell's compiled-in
sources instead. Those are the ones that break silently between releases.
A present symbol still says nothing about behaviour: on GNOME 50
quickSettings._system exists but is not built yet when enable() runs. Only a
running shell catches that.
Used only where present, so absence is not a failure — but presence is not
permission either, and that distinction cost a release's worth of broken
clicks. Clutter.ClickGesture exists from GNOME 49, while only GNOME 50
delivers panel button presses through one; wiring the search button to a
gesture because the class resolved left it inert on 45 to 49. The code asks
PanelMenu.Button what the shell actually does instead, and only the
integration suite can confirm that answer.
Reported per version rather than asserted, so the split stays visible.

methods.comment: Instance methods, checked on the prototype so a rename is caught.

comment: Alternatives, where one form replaced another. mutter 49 introduced
is_maximized() alongside the older get_maximized() flags getter, so the
code copes with both and only needs one to exist.
APIs that look like they should exist and do not. Listed so a future
change cannot reintroduce a call to one without the check failing.
Clutter has no accelerator parser in any supported version — only
keyval_name, in the opposite direction.
